faq_local.q: Hail damaged my Sanger home and horse barn. Can I appraise both in one claim?
faq_local.a: If both structures are covered and your insurer accepts the hail claim, appraisal can address the amount for each. On Sanger-area properties, appraisers commonly inspect home roofs and siding along with metal barn roofing, gutters and trim. Each side's appraiser prices repairs for every structure, and an umpire resolves differences on the amount.

dayton.local_intro: Dayton is a growing Liberty County city along US 90 near the Trinity River, where older homes and small businesses downtown give way to new subdivisions and rural acreage as Houston growth pushes east. Many homes sit on large lots among pines and pastures. A Dayton insurance appraiser often handles hurricane wind, flooding-related and roof claims, as the area has experienced significant storm damage.
dayton.weather: Liberty County faces hurricane winds and severe flooding; Hurricane Harvey in 2017 caused major flooding along the Trinity River near Dayton. Hurricane Beryl in 2024 brought damaging winds and long outages to the region. Falling pines damage roofs during storms, spring thunderstorms produce hail, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes.
dayton.property_mix: Brick and wood-frame homes with composition shingle roofs are common, along with manufactured homes on rural lots. Newer subdivisions feature brick homes with architectural shingles, and farm properties use metal barns and shops.

faq_local.q: A tree fell on my Dayton home during a hurricane. How does appraisal work with my deductible?
faq_local.a: If your insurer accepts that hurricane winds caused the tree to fall on your Dayton home but disagrees on the amount, appraisal can resolve the repair cost for the roof, framing and interior. Your hurricane or named-storm deductible then applies under your policy. Debris removal limits may also affect payment, so review your policy terms carefully.

mont-belvieu.local_intro: Mont Belvieu, in western Chambers County, is known for its vast underground salt-dome storage and petrochemical facilities, while its residential side has grown rapidly with new subdivisions near the Grand Parkway and I-10. Homes are mostly recent construction, with acreage properties on the edges. A Mont Belvieu insurance appraiser often handles hurricane wind, hail and water claims for homes and businesses.
mont-belvieu.weather: Mont Belvieu faces Gulf hurricanes and tropical storms; Hurricane Ike in 2008 and Hurricane Harvey in 2017 brought severe wind and flooding to Chambers County, and Hurricane Beryl in 2024 caused wind damage across the area. Spring storms produce hail and straight-line winds, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes.
mont-belvieu.property_mix: Newer brick homes with composition or architectural shingle roofs dominate subdivisions, while acreage properties include metal barns and shops. Industrial facilities use metal buildings and TPO roofs designed for coastal wind loads.

faq_local.q: My Mont Belvieu home is fairly new. Why was my hurricane wind claim underpaid?
faq_local.a: Even newer Mont Belvieu homes can have disputes over how much of the roof needs replacement, whether matching shingles are available and how interior damage is valued. If your insurer accepts the wind claim but you disagree on the amount, appraisal lets each side's appraiser price the loss, with an umpire resolving differences.

northlake.local_intro: Northlake was a small rural town in southwest Denton County until master-planned communities such as Harvest and Pecan Square transformed it into one of the region's fastest-growing places near I-35W and Texas Motor Speedway. Nearly all homes are new construction on former farmland. A Northlake insurance appraiser often handles hail and wind claims on newer roofs, where scope and matching disputes are common.
northlake.weather: Northlake sits in an active North Texas hail corridor, where spring supercells can produce very large hail, damaging straight-line winds and occasional tornadoes. Open former farmland gives little wind protection to new homes. Heavy rain can flood creeks and detention areas, expansive clay soils shift slabs, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes.
northlake.property_mix: Newer brick, stone and fiber-cement homes feature composition or architectural shingle roofs, with some standing-seam metal accents and impact-resistant shingles. Commercial and logistics buildings near I-35W use flat TPO roofs.

faq_local.q: My Northlake home is only two years old and has hail damage. Will the builder warranty or insurance cover it?
faq_local.a: Builder warranties generally cover defects, not storm damage, so hail damage to your Northlake home is usually an insurance matter. If your insurer accepts the hail claim but disagrees on the amount, appraisal allows each side's appraiser to inspect the roof and price repairs or replacement. An umpire resolves any remaining differences.

cleveland.local_intro: Cleveland lies in northwest Liberty County along US 59, at the edge of the Big Thicket pine country, where an older railroad-town center meets rapidly expanding rural subdivisions and acreage lots. Many homes sit beneath tall pines, and manufactured homes are common on outlying land. A Cleveland insurance appraiser often handles tree-impact, hurricane wind and roof claims after Gulf storms and spring thunderstorms.
cleveland.weather: Cleveland faces hurricane and tropical storm winds that can topple pines across homes and roads; Hurricane Harvey in 2017 brought flooding to the region and Hurricane Beryl in 2024 caused widespread tree damage. Heavy rain floods creeks and low roads. Spring storms bring hail and tornadoes, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes.
cleveland.property_mix: Brick and wood-frame homes with composition shingle roofs are typical, along with manufactured homes and metal-roofed rural houses. Older homes near downtown sit on pier-and-beam foundations, and small businesses use flat or metal roofs.

faq_local.q: Several pines fell on my Cleveland property after a storm. Can appraisal address the full damage?
faq_local.a: If your insurer accepts that the storm caused the trees to fall on covered structures at your Cleveland property, appraisal can resolve disagreements over repair costs for the roof, framing, fences and interiors. Debris and tree removal coverage often has separate limits. Each side's appraiser prices the damage, and an umpire resolves differences.

joshua.local_intro: Joshua is a fast-growing Johnson County city between Burleson and Cleburne along SH 174, where an older town center and rural acreage are giving way to new subdivisions served by the Chisholm Trail Parkway. Many residents own barns or shops alongside their homes. A Joshua insurance appraiser often handles hail and wind claims on newer roofs, older homes and rural outbuildings.
joshua.weather: Johnson County sees frequent spring severe weather, with large hail, damaging straight-line winds and tornadoes; nearby Cleburne was struck by a tornado in May 2013. Heavy rain causes flash flooding on creeks and rural roads. Expansive clay soils shift foundations, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused frozen pipes on homes and farm water systems.
joshua.property_mix: Brick-veneer homes with composition or architectural shingle roofs dominate newer subdivisions, while older homes and manufactured homes appear on rural lots. Barns and shops use standing-seam or exposed-fastener metal roofing.

faq_local.q: Can appraisal help if the insurer says my Joshua roof damage is from wear rather than the storm?
faq_local.a: Appraisal primarily resolves the amount of loss. If your insurer denies that the storm caused any damage to your Joshua roof, the dispute may be about causation, which appraisal may or may not address depending on policy language and Texas law. An appraiser can review the roof evidence and your policy to help you understand your options.

liberty.local_intro: Liberty, the Liberty County seat, sits on the east bank of the Trinity River, with a historic downtown, older neighborhoods under pines and live oaks, and farms and ranches spread across the surrounding bottomland. It is one of the oldest towns in Texas. A Liberty insurance appraiser often handles hurricane wind, flooding-related and tree-impact claims, as river flooding and Gulf storms regularly affect the area.
liberty.weather: Liberty faces hurricane and tropical storm winds, with Hurricane Ike in 2008 and Hurricane Beryl in 2024 causing wind damage in the region. Hurricane Harvey in 2017 caused major flooding along the Trinity River. Falling trees damage roofs during storms, spring thunderstorms bring hail and tornadoes, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes.
liberty.property_mix: Older wood-frame and brick homes, many on pier-and-beam foundations, have composition shingle roofs, along with manufactured homes in rural areas. Farm properties use metal barns, and historic downtown buildings have flat built-up roofs.

faq_local.q: My Liberty home had wind damage and some flooding from the river. How does appraisal handle that?
faq_local.a: Homeowners policies in Liberty usually cover wind damage but exclude rising-water flooding, which falls under separate flood insurance. Appraisal can resolve disagreements over the amount of covered wind damage. Separating wind-related damage from flood damage is often part of the dispute, and an appraiser can help document what each policy should address.

austin.local_intro: Texas's capital blends century-old bungalows in Hyde Park and Travis Heights with high-rise condos downtown, booming tech campuses and sprawling suburban neighborhoods from Circle C to Mueller. Construction costs are high and housing ages vary widely. An Austin insurance appraiser often handles hail and wind claims, ice-storm tree damage and costly water losses in homes, condos and commercial buildings across the city.
austin.weather: Austin faces spring and fall hailstorms, damaging straight-line winds and flash flooding in creeks such as Onion and Shoal; the Halloween 2013 flood hit southeast Austin hard. Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused widespread burst pipes, and the February 2023 ice storm downed countless trees onto homes. Expansive clay soils and wildfire on the western edge add risk.
austin.property_mix: Older bungalows on pier-and-beam foundations have composition or metal roofs, while newer homes use stone, stucco and fiber-cement with architectural shingles or standing-seam metal. Downtown towers and commercial buildings use flat TPO and modified-bitumen roofs.

faq_local.q: Ice storm limbs damaged my Austin roof and fence. Is that something appraisal can handle?
faq_local.a: If your insurer accepts that the ice storm caused tree limbs to damage your Austin roof and fence but disagrees on the amount, appraisal can resolve repair costs. Each side's appraiser documents damage to roofing, gutters, siding and fencing and prices repairs. Debris removal often has separate limits, and an umpire resolves remaining differences.

georgetown.local_intro: Georgetown, the Williamson County seat, pairs a much-admired Victorian courthouse square and Southwestern University with fast growth in communities such as Sun City Texas, Wolf Ranch and Teravista. Many residents are retirees in newer homes, while historic houses line streets near downtown. A Georgetown insurance appraiser often handles hail and wind claims, historic-home repairs and freeze-related water damage.
georgetown.weather: Williamson County experiences spring and fall hailstorms, some producing very large hail, along with damaging straight-line winds and occasional tornadoes. Flash flooding affects the San Gabriel River and creeks during intense rain. Limestone and clay soils affect foundations, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 and the February 2023 ice storm caused burst pipes and tree damage.
georgetown.property_mix: Newer stone, brick and fiber-cement homes with composition or architectural shingle roofs dominate subdivisions, while historic Victorians near the square have wood siding and metal or shingle roofs. Commercial buildings use flat TPO roofs.

faq_local.q: My Sun City home in Georgetown had hail damage. Do HOA requirements affect an appraisal?
faq_local.a: HOA rules in Georgetown communities like Sun City may require specific roofing colors or styles, which can affect matching and replacement scope. If your insurer accepts the hail claim but disagrees on the amount, each side's appraiser considers the materials needed for a reasonably uniform repair. Whether HOA requirements are covered depends on policy language.

pflugerville.local_intro: Pflugerville grew from a German farming settlement into a large suburb northeast of Austin, with communities such as Falcon Pointe, Blackhawk and Avalon spreading along SH 130 and SH 45. Most homes date from the 1990s onward, many now due for roof replacement. A Pflugerville insurance appraiser often handles hail and wind claims, siding and fence damage, and freeze-related water losses.
pflugerville.weather: Pflugerville experiences spring and fall hailstorms and damaging straight-line winds across northern Travis County. Flash flooding can affect Gilleland Creek and drainage channels. Expansive blackland clay soils swell and shrink, cracking slabs and drywall. Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 and the February 2023 ice storm caused burst pipes and heavy tree damage.
pflugerville.property_mix: Two-story brick, stone and fiber-cement homes with composition or architectural shingle roofs are typical, with wood privacy fences on most lots. Retail centers and warehouses along SH 130 use flat TPO roofs.

faq_local.q: My Pflugerville roof claim was approved, but the payment doesn't cover my contractor's bid. What can I do?
faq_local.a: If your insurer accepts the hail or wind claim on your Pflugerville home but the payment falls short of reasonable repair costs, appraisal may be invoked to resolve the amount. Each side's appraiser inspects the roof and prices the repair, considering local labor and material costs. An umpire resolves remaining differences between them.

san-antonio.local_intro: San Antonio stretches from historic King William and Monte Vista mansions to newer master-planned neighborhoods beyond Loop 1604, with military installations, the Medical Center and downtown's River Walk adding commercial variety. Housing ages and materials vary enormously. A San Antonio insurance appraiser often handles hail claims, especially on the north side, along with wind, flash-flood and freeze-related water losses.
san-antonio.weather: San Antonio has a long history of damaging hail, including major hailstorms in April 2016 that damaged many roofs and vehicles on the north side. Spring storms also bring damaging winds. Flash flooding in low-water crossings and creeks is a serious risk, expansive clay soils affect foundations, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused widespread burst pipes.
san-antonio.property_mix: Homes range from historic limestone and wood-frame houses on pier-and-beam foundations to newer stucco and stone homes with composition, architectural shingle or concrete tile roofs. Commercial buildings use flat TPO and modified-bitumen roofs.

faq_local.q: Does a hailstorm on San Antonio's north side affect neighboring homes differently in an appraisal?
faq_local.a: Hail damage can vary from street to street in San Antonio depending on storm path, roof material and age. Appraisal focuses on the specific damage to your property. If your insurer accepts the hail claim but disagrees on the amount, each side's appraiser inspects your roof and prices repairs, and an umpire resolves differences.

corpus-christi.local_intro: Corpus Christi wraps around its namesake bay, with bayfront homes along Ocean Drive, established neighborhoods on the Southside, refineries and port facilities along the ship channel, and beach homes on North Padre Island. Constant salt air and Gulf exposure shape property risks. A Corpus Christi insurance appraiser often handles windstorm, roof, water and commercial claims, including disputes involving TWIA coverage.
corpus-christi.weather: Corpus Christi faces Gulf hurricanes and tropical storms; Hurricane Harvey in 2017 made landfall nearby, causing wind damage in parts of the city and devastating areas just to the northeast. Storm surge threatens low-lying bayfront and island properties. Salt air corrodes roofing, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused frozen and burst pipes.
corpus-christi.property_mix: Single-story brick and stucco homes with composition shingle roofs are typical, with some tile and metal roofs. Island and bayfront homes may be elevated on pilings, and refineries and port facilities use metal and TPO roofs built for coastal wind.

faq_local.q: My Corpus Christi home has TWIA windstorm coverage. Does it have its own appraisal process?
faq_local.a: Yes. Texas Windstorm Insurance Association policies, common in Corpus Christi, include their own dispute procedures and appraisal provisions with specific deadlines that can differ from private homeowners policies. If you disagree with the amount offered for wind damage, review your TWIA notice carefully. An appraiser can explain the process and timelines that apply.

irving.local_intro: Irving sits between Dallas and Fort Worth, home to the Las Colinas business district around Lake Carolyn, the Valley Ranch community and neighborhoods ranging from 1960s ranch homes to newer townhomes. Corporate headquarters, hotels and apartments give the city a large commercial base. An Irving insurance appraiser often handles residential hail claims alongside commercial roof and water disputes.
irving.weather: Irving faces frequent spring hailstorms, damaging straight-line winds and occasional tornadoes typical of the Dallas–Fort Worth area. Heavy rain can cause flooding near the Elm Fork and West Fork of the Trinity River. Expansive clay soils shift foundations, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes in homes and commercial buildings.
irving.property_mix: Single-story brick ranch homes with composition shingle roofs fill older neighborhoods, while Las Colinas and Valley Ranch include larger homes with architectural shingles or tile. Office towers and hotels use flat TPO and modified-bitumen roofs.

faq_local.q: My Irving condo building had hail damage. How does appraisal work for an HOA or condo claim?
faq_local.a: For Irving condos, the HOA's master policy typically covers the building exterior and roof, while unit owners' policies cover interiors and improvements. If the master insurer accepts the hail claim but disagrees on the amount, the association can invoke appraisal. Unit owners may have separate claims for interior damage under their own policies.

mckinney.local_intro: McKinney blends a lively historic downtown square with large master-planned communities such as Craig Ranch, Stonebridge Ranch and Tucker Hill, spreading across north-central Collin County. Older homes near downtown contrast with newer construction to the north and west. A McKinney insurance appraiser often handles hail claims, matching disputes on newer roofs, and water losses in both historic and modern homes.
mckinney.weather: McKinney sits in one of North Texas's most active hail corridors, with spring supercells producing very large hail, damaging straight-line winds and occasional tornadoes. Heavy rain can flood creeks and the East Fork of the Trinity. Expansive clay soils shift foundations, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes in many homes.
mckinney.property_mix: Two-story brick and stone homes with composition or architectural shingle roofs dominate newer communities, with some tile and slate. Historic homes downtown include wood-frame Victorians, and commercial buildings use flat TPO roofs.

faq_local.q: My historic home near downtown McKinney has hail damage. Can appraisal account for its unique features?
faq_local.a: Historic McKinney homes often have wood siding, decorative trim and roofing that require skilled labor and matching materials. If your insurer accepts the hail claim but disagrees on the amount, each side's appraiser documents these features and prices repairs with like kind and quality materials. An umpire resolves differences between the appraisers.

killeen.local_intro: Killeen is a military city shaped by Fort Hood, one of the largest Army installations in the country, with neighborhoods of single-family homes, rental properties and apartments housing soldiers and their families. Many homes are investor-owned rentals, and construction ranges from 1950s houses to newer subdivisions. A Killeen insurance appraiser often handles hail, wind and water claims for owner-occupants and landlords alike.
killeen.weather: Bell County experiences spring storms with large hail, damaging straight-line winds and occasional tornadoes. Heavy rain causes flash flooding along Nolan Creek and other streams. Expansive clay and limestone soils shift foundations, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused widespread frozen and burst pipes in homes and vacant rental properties alike.
killeen.property_mix: Single-story brick-veneer homes with composition shingle roofs are typical, with newer subdivisions using architectural shingles. Duplexes and apartments use pitched shingle roofs, and commercial buildings along US 190 use flat TPO or built-up roofs.

faq_local.q: I own a rental home in Killeen with hail damage. Can I use appraisal as a landlord?
faq_local.a: Yes. Landlord or dwelling fire policies covering Killeen rental properties usually include an appraisal clause. If your insurer accepts the hail claim but disagrees on the amount, each side's appraiser inspects the property and prices repairs, and an umpire resolves differences. Loss of rental income may also be covered depending on your policy.

pasadena.local_intro: Pasadena stretches south from the Houston Ship Channel, where refineries and chemical plants line SH 225, toward residential neighborhoods near Armand Bayou and Clear Lake. Most homes are single-story brick houses built from the 1950s through the 1980s. A Pasadena insurance appraiser often handles hurricane wind, roof and water claims, along with commercial and industrial property disputes.
pasadena.weather: Pasadena faces hurricane winds and flooding; Hurricane Ike in 2008 damaged many roofs, and Hurricane Harvey in 2017 caused widespread flooding across east Harris County. Hurricane Beryl in 2024 brought damaging winds and power outages. Spring thunderstorms produce hail and occasional tornadoes, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes.
pasadena.property_mix: Single-story brick-veneer homes with composition shingle roofs are typical, some on pier-and-beam foundations in older areas. Industrial plants use metal buildings and TPO roofs, and strip centers along Spencer Highway have flat built-up roofs.

faq_local.q: My older Pasadena home needs roof decking replaced after hurricane damage. Will appraisal include that?
faq_local.a: If your insurer accepts the hurricane wind claim on your Pasadena home, appraisal can include damaged or deteriorated decking that must be replaced as part of the covered repair, along with code-required items your policy covers. Each side's appraiser documents the roof and prices the work, and an umpire resolves remaining differences.

college-station.local_intro: Home to Texas A&M University and Kyle Field, College Station has a large share of student rentals, duplexes and apartments near campus and Northgate, alongside family neighborhoods such as Pebble Creek and Castlegate to the south. Investor-owned properties are common. A College Station insurance appraiser often handles hail and wind claims on rentals and family homes, plus water losses in multifamily buildings.
college-station.weather: Brazos County sees spring thunderstorms with hail, damaging straight-line winds and occasional tornadoes. Remnants of Gulf hurricanes can bring heavy rain and gusty winds inland, as Hurricane Harvey did in 2017. Expansive clay soils shift foundations, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes in homes and apartment complexes.
college-station.property_mix: Brick-veneer homes with composition or architectural shingle roofs are common, with duplexes and apartments using pitched shingle roofs. University buildings and commercial centers along Texas Avenue use flat TPO and modified-bitumen roofs.

faq_local.q: I own several duplex rentals in College Station damaged by hail. Can I appraise them together?
faq_local.a: Each College Station property may be a separate claim depending on how your policies are written, though a single policy can cover multiple locations. If your insurer accepts the hail damage but disagrees on the amount, appraisal can be invoked for each disputed claim. Each side's appraiser prices repairs, and an umpire resolves differences.

league-city.local_intro: League City sits between Houston and Galveston along I-45 and Clear Creek, with marina communities such as South Shore Harbour, master-planned neighborhoods like Tuscan Lakes and an older historic district shaded by live oaks. Proximity to Clear Lake and Galveston Bay shapes storm risk. A League City insurance appraiser often handles hurricane wind, roof and water claims after Gulf storms and heavy rains.
league-city.weather: League City faces hurricanes and tropical storms; Hurricane Ike in 2008 caused widespread wind damage, Hurricane Harvey in 2017 brought severe flooding along Clear Creek, and Hurricane Beryl in 2024 damaged roofs and trees. Spring storms produce hail and straight-line winds, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes.
league-city.property_mix: Two-story brick and stucco homes with composition or architectural shingle roofs dominate newer subdivisions, with some tile roofs. Older homes in the historic district are wood-frame, and marina-area buildings use metal roofing.

faq_local.q: Does League City's location mean I have separate windstorm coverage for appraisal?
faq_local.a: Some League City properties have wind coverage through a private homeowners policy, while others may carry separate windstorm coverage, depending on location and insurer. Each policy has its own appraisal clause and deductibles. An appraiser can help determine which policy covers your wind damage and explain the appraisal process for that policy.

edinburg.local_intro: Edinburg, the Hidalgo County seat, is home to the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley and a fast-growing mix of subdivisions, medical facilities and commercial development north of McAllen. Older homes near downtown contrast with newer stucco neighborhoods. An Edinburg insurance appraiser often handles wind, hail and flooding-related claims for homeowners, landlords near campus and commercial property owners.
landmarks: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
edinburg.weather: The Rio Grande Valley faces tropical storms and hurricanes; Hurricane Hanna in July 2020 brought damaging winds and widespread flooding to Hidalgo County. Flat terrain causes slow drainage and neighborhood flooding during heavy rain. Spring storms can produce large hail, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused frozen pipes in homes built for mild winters.
edinburg.property_mix: Single-story stucco, brick and concrete-block homes with composition shingle roofs are typical, with some flat roof sections. University buildings and commercial centers use flat TPO and built-up roofs, and warehouses use metal panels.

faq_local.q: My Edinburg home was damaged by wind and flooding from a tropical storm. How does appraisal work?
faq_local.a: Homeowners policies in Edinburg typically cover wind damage but exclude rising-water flooding, which requires separate flood insurance. If your insurer accepts the wind claim but disagrees on the amount, appraisal can resolve the cost of repairs to the roof, windows and wind-related interior damage. An appraiser can help separate wind and flood damage.

bryan.local_intro: Bryan, the Brazos County seat, has a revitalized historic downtown of brick storefronts, older neighborhoods with craftsman and Victorian homes, and newer subdivisions extending north and east. It shares a metro area with College Station and hosts a Blinn College campus. A Bryan insurance appraiser often handles hail and wind claims on older homes, historic commercial buildings and newer houses.
bryan.weather: Brazos County experiences spring thunderstorms with hail, damaging straight-line winds and occasional tornadoes. Remnants of Gulf tropical systems sometimes bring heavy rain and wind, as Hurricane Harvey did in 2017. Expansive clay soils cause foundation movement in older and newer homes, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes across the area.
bryan.property_mix: Older wood-frame and brick homes, many on pier-and-beam foundations, have composition shingle roofs. Newer subdivisions feature brick homes with architectural shingles, and historic downtown buildings use flat built-up roofs over masonry.

faq_local.q: My historic home in Bryan needs specialized repairs after a storm. Can appraisal help?
faq_local.a: If your insurer accepts the storm claim on your Bryan home but disagrees on the amount, appraisal can help price repairs to wood siding, trim, windows and roofing with materials of like kind and quality. Each side's appraiser documents the home's features and prices the work, and an umpire resolves differences between them.

longview.local_intro: Longview, the Gregg County seat, grew from the East Texas oil boom into a regional center for manufacturing, healthcare and retail, with LeTourneau University and neighborhoods of older homes beneath tall pines. Newer subdivisions extend toward Pine Tree and Spring Hill. A Longview insurance appraiser often handles tree-impact, hail and wind claims on homes and commercial and industrial buildings.
longview.weather: East Texas spring storms bring hail, damaging straight-line winds and tornadoes to Gregg County. Saturated soils make tall pines prone to falling on homes. Heavy rain can flood creeks feeding the Sabine River, and remnants of Gulf hurricanes occasionally reach the area. Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 and periodic ice storms caused frozen pipes and fallen limbs.
longview.property_mix: Brick and wood-frame homes with composition shingle roofs are common, with older homes on pier-and-beam foundations. Manufacturing plants and warehouses use metal buildings and TPO roofs, and downtown buildings have flat built-up roofs.

faq_local.q: A pine tree fell through my Longview roof. Can appraisal resolve a dispute over the repair cost?
faq_local.a: If your insurer accepts that the storm caused the tree to fall on your Longview home but disagrees on the amount, appraisal can resolve the cost to repair the roof, framing, ceilings and interiors. Each side's appraiser documents the damage and prices repairs. Tree removal limits may apply, and an umpire resolves differences.

flower-mound.local_intro: Flower Mound is a large, affluent Denton County town between Grapevine Lake and Lewisville Lake, known for its namesake prairie mound, preserved open space and neighborhoods such as Bridlewood, Wellington and Canyon Falls. Most homes are two-story brick houses built from the 1980s onward. A Flower Mound insurance appraiser often handles hail claims on large roofs and costly interior water damage.
flower-mound.weather: Flower Mound sits in an active North Texas hail corridor, where spring supercells can produce very large hail, damaging straight-line winds and occasional tornadoes. Heavy rain can flood creeks feeding the two lakes. Expansive clay soils shift foundations, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes and extensive interior water damage in many large homes.
flower-mound.property_mix: Two-story brick and stone homes with composition or architectural shingle roofs dominate, along with some tile and slate on larger homes. Retail and office buildings along FM 2499 and FM 1171 use flat TPO roofs.

faq_local.q: My Flower Mound home had a burst pipe during a freeze. Can appraisal help with the water damage claim?
faq_local.a: If your insurer accepts that freeze-related water damage to your Flower Mound home is covered but disagrees on the amount, appraisal can resolve the cost to repair flooring, drywall, cabinets and other affected areas. Each side's appraiser documents and prices the damage, and an umpire resolves differences. Mold coverage may have separate limits.

san-marcos.local_intro: San Marcos, the Hays County seat, is home to Texas State University and the spring-fed San Marcos River, with student housing near campus, older neighborhoods around the downtown square and newer communities such as Kissing Tree and Blanco Vista. Rental properties are common. A San Marcos insurance appraiser often handles flood-adjacent water, hail and wind claims for owners and landlords.
san-marcos.weather: San Marcos lies in Flash Flood Alley, and the Memorial Day 2015 flood on the Blanco River caused severe damage in the area. Spring and fall storms bring hail and damaging straight-line winds. Expansive clay soils shift foundations, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 and the February 2023 ice storm caused burst pipes and fallen trees.
san-marcos.property_mix: Older wood-frame homes on pier-and-beam foundations mix with newer brick, stone and fiber-cement homes with composition shingle roofs. Student apartments use pitched shingle roofs, and commercial buildings along I-35 use flat TPO roofs.

faq_local.q: My San Marcos rental property had water damage from a storm. Is that covered and can appraisal help?
faq_local.a: Water entering through storm-damaged roofs or windows is often covered, while rising floodwater usually requires separate flood insurance. If your insurer accepts the claim on your San Marcos rental but disagrees on the amount, appraisal can resolve repair costs. Loss of rental income may also be covered depending on your policy.

spring.local_intro: Spring is a large unincorporated area of north Harris County, centered on the historic shops of Old Town Spring and surrounded by neighborhoods such as Gleannloch Farms, Klein and Champion Forest. Most homes date from the 1970s onward under heavy tree canopy. A Spring insurance appraiser often handles hurricane wind, tree-impact and roof claims, along with water losses after floods and freezes.
spring.weather: Spring faces hurricane winds and flooding; Hurricane Harvey in 2017 caused severe flooding along Spring Creek and Cypress Creek, and Hurricane Beryl in 2024 downed trees and power lines across north Harris County. The May 2024 derecho caused wind damage in the region. Spring storms bring hail, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 burst pipes.
spring.property_mix: Two-story brick homes with composition or architectural shingle roofs are typical, many under mature pines and oaks. Older homes in Old Town Spring are wood-frame, and commercial centers along I-45 use flat TPO roofs.

faq_local.q: Hurricane Beryl dropped a tree on my Spring home. How long do I have to request appraisal?
faq_local.a: Deadlines to invoke appraisal depend on your policy language, and Texas law sets timelines for claim handling and lawsuits. For your Spring home, review the appraisal clause and any written notices from your insurer. An appraiser can help you understand the deadlines that apply so you can act promptly if you disagree with the amount offered.

cedar-hill.local_intro: Cedar Hill sits on the highest ground in Dallas County, where the Balcones escarpment rises toward Joe Pool Lake and Cedar Hill State Park, giving the city hilly terrain, wooded lots and views uncommon in North Texas. Homes range from 1970s ranch houses to newer subdivisions. A Cedar Hill insurance appraiser often handles hail and wind claims on exposed hillside homes and water losses after freezes.
cedar-hill.weather: Cedar Hill's elevated terrain exposes homes to strong winds during spring storms, which also bring large hail and occasional tornadoes. Heavy rain can cause runoff and erosion on slopes and flooding along creeks. Expansive clay soils shift foundations, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused frozen and burst pipes in many homes.
cedar-hill.property_mix: Brick-veneer homes with composition or architectural shingle roofs dominate, with some stone homes on larger wooded lots. Retail centers along US 67 use flat TPO or built-up roofs, and lakeside homes may include decks and retaining walls.

faq_local.q: My Cedar Hill home on a hill seems to get more wind damage. Does that affect an appraisal?
faq_local.a: Homes on elevated or exposed lots in Cedar Hill can experience stronger winds and more extensive roof damage. Appraisal focuses on the actual damage to your property, regardless of neighbors' claims. If your insurer accepts the wind claim but disagrees on the amount, each side's appraiser prices repairs, and an umpire resolves differences.

the-colony.local_intro: Occupying a peninsula on the eastern shore of Lewisville Lake, The Colony began as a planned community in the 1970s and now combines those original neighborhoods with newer development at Austin Ranch and the Grandscape entertainment district along SH 121. Many older homes carry aging roofs and plumbing. Hail, wind and water losses in homes and lakeside properties are the disputes most often brought to The Colony insurance appraiser.
the-colony.weather: The Colony sits in North Texas hail country, where spring storms produce large hail, damaging straight-line winds and occasional tornadoes. Lewisville Lake's open water can intensify winds reaching shoreline homes. Heavy rain can cause flooding near the lake, expansive clay soils shift foundations, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused burst pipes.
the-colony.property_mix: Single-story brick homes with composition shingle roofs fill the original 1970s neighborhoods, while Austin Ranch and newer areas feature two-story homes and apartments. Grandscape's retail buildings use flat TPO roofs.

faq_local.q: My 1970s home in The Colony has hail damage and old roof decking. Will appraisal cover decking replacement?
faq_local.a: If your insurer accepts the hail claim on your home in The Colony, appraisal can include decking replacement when it is damaged or must be replaced to complete the covered repair, depending on your policy and code requirements. Each side's appraiser inspects the roof and prices the work, and an umpire resolves differences.

weslaco.local_intro: Weslaco is a mid-Valley city in Hidalgo County along I-2, rooted in citrus agriculture and home to research facilities, a historic downtown and growing subdivisions. Many homes are single-story stucco or brick houses, with packing sheds and agricultural buildings on the city's edges. A Weslaco insurance appraiser often handles wind, hail and flooding-related claims after tropical storms and severe weather.
weslaco.weather: The Rio Grande Valley faces tropical storms and hurricanes; Hurricane Hanna in July 2020 brought damaging winds and widespread flooding to Hidalgo County. Flat terrain and slow drainage cause neighborhood flooding during heavy rain. Spring storms can produce large hail, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused frozen pipes and citrus damage.
weslaco.property_mix: Single-story stucco, brick and concrete-block homes with composition shingle roofs are typical, with some flat roof sections. Packing sheds and agricultural buildings use metal roofing, and commercial strips along I-2 use flat built-up roofs.

faq_local.q: My Weslaco home was damaged by Hurricane Hanna winds. Can appraisal still help if the claim was paid?
faq_local.a: If your Weslaco claim was paid but you believe the amount is too low, appraisal may still be available depending on your policy terms and any deadlines. Each side's appraiser inspects the damage and prices repairs, and an umpire resolves differences. Review your policy and any correspondence from your insurer to understand the timelines that apply.

hurst.local_intro: Hurst is an established mid-cities suburb in northeast Tarrant County, anchored by North East Mall and neighborhoods of brick ranch homes built mostly in the 1950s through 1980s. Many houses now carry aging roofs, older plumbing and mature trees. A Hurst insurance appraiser often handles hail and wind claims, tree damage and water losses in homes and commercial properties along SH 183 and Loop 820.
hurst.weather: Hurst faces frequent spring hailstorms, damaging straight-line winds and occasional tornadoes typical of the Mid-Cities. Heavy rain can cause flooding along local creeks. Expansive clay soils shift foundations, especially in older homes on pier-and-beam or early slab construction, and Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 caused widespread frozen and burst pipes.
hurst.property_mix: Single-story brick-veneer ranch homes with composition shingle roofs are typical, many with replaced architectural shingles. North East Mall and retail centers use flat TPO and modified-bitumen roofs, and some older homes have pier-and-beam foundations.

faq_local.q: My Hurst home has an older roof with hail damage. Will the insurer only pay actual cash value?
faq_local.a: That depends on your policy. Some Hurst homeowners policies pay replacement cost with depreciation released after repairs, while others pay actual cash value for roofs. In appraisal, both appraisers can determine replacement cost and actual cash value as needed, and an umpire resolves differences. Your policy terms determine how the payment is calculated.
